newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 14.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The Dow industrials fell 160.48 to 6,878.89, the largest point drop since July 15. The yield on the 30-year Treasury bond rose to 6.96 percent, the highest level in nearly six months.
* Retail sales rose 0.8 percent in February, but initial jobless claims were lower.
* The Mississippi Supreme Court ruled that the first state Medicaid suit seeking to recoup health care costs of smokers can go to trial.
* Wal-Mart's Canadian stores resumed sales on Cuban-made pajamas.
* Bell Atlantic and DSC Communications settled their multibillion antitrust suit against Lucent Technologies.
* Travelers Group could be the first company to win government approval to contribute stock options to employees' 401(k) accounts.
* Grand Metropolitan names Dennis Malamatinas chief executive of Burger King, a replacement seen to reflect disappointment with international growth.
* Ford extends Chairman Alex Trotman's contract by 18 months.
* Delta Airlines hired Cordiant Plc's Saatchi & Saatchi to handle its $100 million account.
* Mutual-fund groups say yesterday's 160-point drop in Dow Jones Industrial Average did not lead to major redemptions by investors.
* Luby's Cafeteria President and Chief Executive John Edward Curtis Jr committed suicide.
* Apple is cutting its product line and internal red-tape as part of a cost-cutting effort.
* FDIC Chairman Ricki Helfer said she is planning to resign by June.
* Credit-card delinquencies rose to 3.72 percent of accounts in the fourth quarter, an industry group said.

* Heard on the Street: The "Dogs of the Dow" will be woofing a slightly different tune following the just-announced changes in the stocks in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Some investors claim to have had success by buying the Dow's so-called dogs at the end of each year, holding them for a year, and then repeating the exercise.
* Credit markets: The resilience of the American consumer fueled fears of an imminent interest rate increase and caused the bond markets to slump.
